items.question: What does Ruth Riley do for the Miami Heat?
items.answer: Ruth Riley, who now goes by Ruth Hunter, is the Miami Heat's Senior Director of Team Development, a role the Heat announced in August 2022. She first joined the Heat as a broadcast analyst.

items.question: Which WNBA teams did Ruth Riley play for?
items.answer: Ruth Riley played 13 WNBA seasons, from 2001 to 2013, for the Miami Sol, Detroit Shock, San Antonio Silver Stars, Chicago Sky and Atlanta Dream. She won WNBA championships with Detroit in 2003 and 2006 and was the 2003 WNBA Finals MVP.

items.question: How tall is Ruth Riley?
items.answer: Basketball-Reference lists Ruth Riley at 6 feet 5 inches; other listings have her at 6 feet 4 inches. She played center.

items.question: Where did Ruth Riley play college basketball?
items.answer: Ruth Riley played at Notre Dame. As a senior in 2001 she led the Fighting Irish to the NCAA championship, was named Most Outstanding Player of the Final Four and won the Naismith Player of the Year award.

items.question: What were Ruth Riley's career averages?
items.answer: Ruth Riley averaged 6.3 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 387 WNBA regular-season games from 2001 to 2013. Her best scoring season was 2004, at 11.1 points per game for Detroit.

items.question: How old is Ruth Riley?
items.answer: Ruth Riley was born August 28, 1979, in Ransom, Kansas.

items.question: Is Ruth Riley in the Hall of Fame?
items.answer: Yes. Ruth Riley was inducted into the Women's Basketball Hall of Fame in 2019.
